key_insight: A deep-learning reconstructed accelerated whole-body diffusion MRI cut scan time by 37% while preserving image quality and lesion ADC estimates in metastatic prostate cancer.
clinical_relevance: This suggests faster whole-body staging and follow-up imaging may be feasible without sacrificing the quantitative measures clinicians use to assess disease burden.
method: Prospective single-centre study at 1.5T in two patient cohorts.
Cohort 1: blinded radiologist image-quality scoring across four body stations using a 4-point Likert scale.
Cohort 2: ADC comparison in hypercellular bone metastases between standard and accelerated DL WB-DWI.
evidence_signal: Across 30 patients, image quality remained good-to-excellent and ADC values showed no significant difference between standard and accelerated protocols, with agreement assessed using Wilcoxon tests and Bland-Altman analysis.
watch_item: Results come from a small, single-centre study, so broader validation is needed before routine implementation across scanners, sites, and patient populations.
paper_title: Evaluation of accelerated whole-body diffusion weighted imaging with deep learning reconstruction in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: assessment of image quality and ADC estimates.
